comment: Weekly doctrine-build additions. Appended by the scheduled doctrine-database builder. Each entry is a LibrarySource (see lib/military-library.ts). Never edit military-library.generated.json directly — new public documents go here. lib/military-library.ts merges these sources after the generated catalog and drops any entry whose id or url duplicates the catalog or an earlier addition.

sources.title: Influence and Escalation
sources.author: CSIS Project on Nuclear Issues (Rebecca Hersman)
sources.notes: Examines how state and non-state actors covertly manipulate information to shape strategic outcomes, and the escalation risks that come with influence operations — grounds IO threat framing beyond doctrine definitions.

sources.title: Agentic Warfare and the Future of Military Operations
sources.author: CSIS Futures Lab (Benjamin Jensen)
sources.notes: Assesses how autonomous, AI-driven "agentic" systems are reshaping battlefield decision cycles and command relationships — relevant to how information officers frame AI-enabled C2 risk to commanders.

sources.title: Rethinking the Napoleonic Staff
sources.author: CSIS Futures Lab (Benjamin Jensen, Matthew Strohmeyer)
sources.notes: Argues the 19th-century staff model cannot keep pace with AI-accelerated decision cycles and proposes a redesigned staff structure — directly bears on how IO/OIE cells should be organized within a modern staff.

sources.title: How Russia Is Reshaping Command and Control for AI-Enabled Warfare
sources.author: CSIS Wadhwani AI Center (Kateryna Bondar)
sources.notes: First installment of a CSIS series on Russian military AI; details how Russia is adapting its C2 architecture under wartime pressure — a current threat-side baseline for adversary AI-enabled C2 and EW/ISR integration.

sources.title: The Geometry of Coercion: Tracking the PRC's Maritime and Air Pressure on Taiwan
sources.author: CSIS Futures Lab (Jose M. Macias III, Benjamin Jensen)
sources.notes: Introduces a spatial-temporal method for tracking PRC gray-zone maritime and air pressure on Taiwan since 2020 — a quantitative model for detecting and messaging against sub-threshold coercion.

sources.title: Signals in the Swarm: The Data Behind China's Maritime Gray Zone Campaign Near Taiwan
sources.author: CSIS Futures Lab (Jose M. Macias III, Benjamin Jensen)
sources.notes: Data-driven analysis of Chinese maritime gray-zone activity near Taiwan, offering a quantitative framework for characterizing sub-threshold signaling campaigns across the joint force.

sources.title: Partners, Not Proxies: Capacity Building in Hybrid Warfare
sources.author: CSIS (Melissa Dalton, Hijab Shah)
sources.notes: Assesses how the U.S. and partners can build partner-nation capacity against Russian, Iranian, and Chinese hybrid-warfare toolkits — background on adversary gray-zone playbooks for IO planners.

sources.title: Chronology of Possible Chinese Gray Area and Hybrid Warfare Operations
sources.author: CSIS Burke Chair in Strategy (Anthony H. Cordesman, Grace Hwang)
sources.notes: A working chronology cataloguing Chinese gray-zone, hybrid, and multi-domain actions — a reference dataset for tracking adversary information/influence activity over time.
